text.en:
Rani measured the table with her hand span and got 8. Her father measured it and got 6.
"Why do we get different answers?" she asked.
"Our hands are different sizes," said her father. "That is why we need the same unit for everyone."

To measure means to compare with a fixed unit. Hand spans, feet and steps give different answers for different people.
So all over the world we use standard units. The SI unit of length is the metre (m).
Shorter lengths are in centimetres (cm) and millimetres (mm); longer distances are in kilometres (km). 1 m = 100 cm, 1 cm = 10 mm and 1 km = 1000 m.
To measure with a ruler: place the zero mark at one end, keep the ruler straight along the length, and read from straight above the other end.
A measuring tape is used for curved or long things. A thread can measure a curved line: lay it along the line, then straighten it and measure.
Hand spans and steps give different answers for different people, so we need standard units.
The standard unit of length is the metre. A small length is in centimetres or millimetres.
One metre is one hundred centimetres. One centimetre is ten millimetres. One kilometre is one thousand metres.
Put the zero mark at one end, keep the ruler straight, and read from straight above.

problem.en: A pencil is 15 cm long. How many millimetres is that?

text.en: We know that 1 cm is 10 mm.

why.en: This is the link between the two units.
Multiply to change a bigger unit to a smaller one.

text.en: 15 times 10 is 150, so the pencil is 150 mm.

why.en: Check: the answer is a bigger number in the smaller unit.

prompt.en: A classmate measures a book with the ruler starting at the 1 cm mark and reads 21 cm at the other end. What is the real length?

requiredIdeas.en: The ruler did not start at zero.
The real length is 21 cm minus 1 cm, which is 20 cm.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking the last reading is always the length.

points.en: Standard units give the same answer for everyone.
The SI unit of length is the metre.
Start at zero, keep the ruler straight and read from above.
